messages:
maria: Hey - ran into a weird one during onboarding sample app. Streaming responses from the hosted API sometimes drop a final JSON chunk after a reconnect, leaving client-side parser waiting. Repro steps below.

ben: ugh. Can you paste the minimal repro? is this EventSource or fetch streaming?

maria: EventSource (browser) and node-fetch stream in our sampleapp. Steps: 1) start stream with prompt that yields multi-chunk JSON objects 2) flip network (simulate flaky wifi) 3) client reconnects with Last-Event-ID but occasionally final chunk is duplicated or missing, causing parse error.

sam: do you have logs from the server side around the reconnect? might be a reassembly issue where last-frame ack isn't applied.

maria: Server logs show two close events and a new session. I see this pattern in the client console: 

```
received chunk: {"id":1,"data":"{\"text\":\"Hello\"}"
received chunk: {"id":2,"data":"{\"text\":\"Wo"
// disconnect occurs here
reconnect with Last-Event-ID: 2
received chunk: {"id":2,"data":"rld\"}"}
received chunk: {"id":3,"data":"{\"text\":\"Bye\"}"
```

maria: sometimes the "rld" piece arrives as a separate re-emitted fragment and the client ends up assembling 2 and 2' -> duplicate or interleaved.

ben: interesting. Might be our resume-token semantics. Event IDs shouldn't be treated as atomic "message fullness" markers if we chunk mid-json. We need to ensure the server only advances last-event-id when a full logical payload is flushed.

sam: agreed. On the runtime side we emit fragments as they arrive. We could add a small framing header for logical boundary, e.g., send `: boundary <token>` when a full message completes so clients can resume idempotently.

maria: that would help. For SDK parity, our Python/Go SDKs reassemble differently: python buffers until newline, go tries to parse per chunk. This explains why mobile repros look worse.

ben: we should add a compatibility note in the sample app and quickstart: "use provided reassembly helper until server framing is stable". Also file a short ticket to normalize last-event-id semantics.

sam: quick mitigation: client can detect duplicate suffixes by storing the last-seen fragment hash per event id. Ugly but low-risk until we change server.

maria: will try that hack in the sample app and push a patch. Can we also add a small test harness to our onboarding repo that simulates network flaps and asserts JSON parse completeness?

ben: yes please. Add it under sample-app/test/stream-flap.js and include an env flag to run locally. I can review.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: sample-app/dev -> staging (job 7843) :rocket:

maria: pushed the fix. Patch includes: 1) event-id buffering in browser sample, 2) test harness that toggles net via chrome-headless, 3) README note about SDK reassembly.

ben: quick look - code is fine. Can you add an inline comment explaining why we hash fragments? future us will ask.

maria: added. leaving note for runtime: consider a server-side framing header or atomic event flush. Filing runtime ticket now.

sam: filed TKT-3412: "streaming: atomic logical-message boundaries for SSE resume" with logs attached.

maria: thanks. marking this thread for follow-up when runtime change is queued. :thumbsup:
